identity.name: Auto-Revoke OAuth Tokens on Connected-App Abuse — Salesforce Bulk Export -> Playbook Revoke + Forced Re-Auth (F5)
identity.summary: A stolen Salesforce Connected-App OAuth token runs a high-volume Bulk API export then deletes the query jobs (Salesloft Drift abuse; source names no actor). An XSOAR playbook auto-revokes the access and refresh token; a replay with the stale token returns 401 invalid_token. The correlation stitches export -> erase -> revoke -> 401 into one incident asserting the token is dead: F5 closed-loop KPI.
identity.description: This card validates the CLOSED-LOOP RESPONSE half of the Salesloft Drift OAuth-abuse story (the detection half is SIM-CLOUD-006 / TTP-2026-0111). A threat actor — the cited Unit 42 brief deliberately does not attribute the campaign to any named group — abused compromised OAuth credentials for the Drift Connected App (Aug 8-18 2025) to run rapid, high-throughput Salesforce Bulk API exports over an async Python client (user-agent 'Python/3.11 aiohttp/3.12.15'), then deleted the SOQL query jobs (UniqueQuery events) to hide their tracks. Salesloft's remediation was to proactively revoke all active access and refresh tokens for the Drift application, forcing re-authentication for affected admins. This scenario models that remediation as an automated Cortex XSOAR playbook and PROVES it closed the loop rather than merely alerting: (1) the mass-export behavioral anomaly on the Connected-App token is the trigger; (2) the query-job deletion is the anti-forensics tell; (3) the playbook revokes the access AND refresh token for the exact connected_app + oauth_token_id and requires forced re-auth for affected admins; (4) a replay call carrying the revoked token returns HTTP 401 with error_code invalid_token. A correlation rule fuses all four stages on the shared connected_app + oauth_token_id into a single incident whose terminal assertion is that the token is dead. Emphasis is CORRELATION-TERMINAL (methodology family F5): the DC proves not just that Cortex saw the abuse but that the automated response executed and verifiably killed the abused grant, with a blast-radius negative test confirming benign Connected Apps were left untouched.

campaigns: Salesloft Drift Connected-App OAuth abuse against Salesforce instances (August 2025)

techniques.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-CLOUD-007 — Connected-App OAuth token abuse with automated XSOAR token-revoke closed-loop validation.

prerequisites.description: A SaaS/CASB collector is ingesting Salesforce event-monitoring / audit telemetry into cloud_audit_logs so Bulk API jobs, OAuth token-revocation, and API-auth (401) events are queryable.
An XSOAR auto-revoke playbook is wired to the Connected-App-abuse trigger with a Salesforce integration credential authorised to revoke tokens and force re-auth.

payload.code:
# SAFE-MODE: all calls target 127.0.0.1 and write local markers; no real
# Salesforce tenant is touched. Models the abuse -> automated-revoke closed loop.
set -euo pipefail
EXFIL_UA="Python/3.11 aiohttp/3.12.15"
TOKEN_ID="0Ci5SIMDRIFTTOKEN"
# (1) high-volume Bulk API mass export on the trusted Connected-App token
for OBJ in Account Contact Case Opportunity; do
  curl -s --max-time 5 -A "$EXFIL_UA" -X POST "https://127.0.0.1/services/data/v61.0/jobs/query" \
    -d "{\"operation\":\"query\",\"query\":\"SELECT Id FROM ${OBJ}\"}" -o /dev/null 2>/dev/null || true
  echo "SAFE-MODE export object=${OBJ} rows=250000 ua=${EXFIL_UA} token=${TOKEN_ID}" > "/tmp/sf-007-export-${OBJ}.marker"
done
# (2) export-then-erase: delete the query jobs (anti-forensics)
for OBJ in Account Contact Case Opportunity; do
  curl -s --max-time 5 -A "$EXFIL_UA" -X DELETE "https://127.0.0.1/services/data/v61.0/jobs/query/750SIM${OBJ}" -o /dev/null 2>/dev/null || true
done
# (3) XSOAR auto-revoke playbook: revoke access + refresh token, force re-auth
echo "SAFE-MODE revoke token=${TOKEN_ID} types=access,refresh source=cortex-xsoar-playbook" > /tmp/sf-007-revoke.marker
echo "SAFE-MODE force_reauth connected_app=Drift affected_admins=applied" > /tmp/sf-007-reauth.marker
# (4) replay with the revoked token -> expect 401 invalid_token (closed-loop proof)
curl -s --max-time 5 -A "$EXFIL_UA" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN_ID}" \
  "https://127.0.0.1/services/data/v61.0/jobs/query" -o /dev/null 2>/dev/null || true
echo "SAFE-MODE replay token=${TOKEN_ID} response_status=401 error_code=invalid_token" > /tmp/sf-007-replay-401.marker
echo cortexsim-cloud-007-auto-revoke-closed-loop-complete

input_variables.name: CONNECTED_APP
input_variables.description: The abused Salesforce Connected App whose OAuth grant the playbook revokes.

expected_artifacts.description: Salesforce Bulk API query jobs across Account/Contact/Case/Opportunity carrying the automation exfil user-agent on one Connected-App token, followed by deleteJob events.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: cloud_service = "salesforce" and api_type = "Bulk" and user_agent = "Python/3.11 aiohttp/3.12.15"

expected_artifacts.description: An XSOAR-sourced OAuth token-revocation event revoking both the access and refresh token for the offending Connected App, plus a forced-re-auth requirement for affected admins.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: event_type = "OAuthToken" and operation in ("revokeAccessToken", "revokeRefreshToken") and action_source = "cortex-xsoar-playbook"

expected_artifacts.description: A replay API call carrying the revoked token that Salesforce rejects with HTTP 401 invalid_token — the closed-loop proof the revoke landed.

abiocs.name: Connected-App OAuth Token Mass-Export Deviation Triggering Auto-Revoke
abiocs.description: A Salesforce Connected-App OAuth token whose learned baseline is low-volume, narrow-object scheduled Bulk API jobs suddenly runs a high-volume export across Account/Contact/Case/Opportunity from the automation exfil user-agent. This is the behavioral trigger the XSOAR auto-revoke playbook responds to. The ABIOC anchors the deviation to the Connected-App identity (connected_app + oauth_token_id) rather than to any known-bad string — no consent, MFA, or interactive login event exists to alert on, so the volume/object-diversity deviation on the trusted token is the signal.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter cloud_service = "salesforce" and event_type = "BulkApi" and api_type = "Bulk"
| filter operation in ("query", "queryAll")
| filter object_name in ("Account", "Contact", "Case", "Opportunity")
| comp sum(rows_processed) as run_rows, count_distinct(object_name) as run_objects by connected_app, integration_user, oauth_token_id, user_agent
| filter run_rows >= 50000 and run_objects >= 3
| sort desc run_rows
| fields connected_app, integration_user, oauth_token_id, user_agent, run_rows, run_objects
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned Connected-App integration baseline (low-volume scheduled Bulk API on a narrow object set) -> already-consented OAuth token drives a high-volume multi-object export, anchored to the connected_app + oauth_token_id that owns the grant. This anomaly is the automation trigger for the token-revoke playbook.

xql_queries.name: Salesforce Query-Job Deletion Anti-Forensics by Exfiltration Token
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| filter cloud_service = "salesforce" and api_type = "Bulk" and operation = "deleteJob"
| filter user_agent = "Python/3.11 aiohttp/3.12.15"
| comp count() as deleted_jobs by connected_app, integration_user, oauth_token_id, user_agent
| filter deleted_jobs >= 1
| sort desc deleted_jobs
| fields connected_app, integration_user, oauth_token_id, deleted_jobs

xql_queries.name: SOAR Playbook OAuth Access and Refresh Token Revocation for Connected App
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| filter cloud_service = "salesforce" and event_type = "OAuthToken"
| filter operation in ("revokeAccessToken", "revokeRefreshToken", "revokeToken")
| filter action_source = "cortex-xsoar-playbook"
| comp count_distinct(token_type) as revoked_token_types, count() as revoke_events by connected_app, oauth_token_id, playbook_name
| filter revoked_token_types >= 2
| sort desc revoke_events
| fields connected_app, oauth_token_id, playbook_name, revoked_token_types, revoke_events

xql_queries.name: Forced Re-Authentication Requirement Applied to Affected Connected-App Admins
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| filter cloud_service = "salesforce" and event_type = "SessionSecurity"
| filter operation = "forceReauth" and action_source = "cortex-xsoar-playbook"
| comp count() as forced_reauth_events by connected_app, affected_user
| filter forced_reauth_events >= 1
| sort desc forced_reauth_events
| fields connected_app, affected_user, forced_reauth_events

xql_queries.name: Revoked-Token Replay Returns 401 invalid_token Closed-Loop Proof
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| filter cloud_service = "salesforce" and event_type = "ApiAuth"
| filter user_agent = "Python/3.11 aiohttp/3.12.15"
| filter response_status = 401 and error_code = "invalid_token"
| comp count() as rejected_calls, max(_time) as last_rejection by connected_app, integration_user, oauth_token_id
| filter rejected_calls >= 1
| sort desc rejected_calls
| fields connected_app, integration_user, oauth_token_id, rejected_calls, last_rejection

correlation_rules.name: Connected-App OAuth Token Abuse Auto-Revoke Closed-Loop Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(Connected-App OAuth Token Mass-Export Deviation Triggering Auto-Revoke) AND XQL(Salesforce Query-Job Deletion Anti-Forensics by Exfiltration Token) AND XQL(SOAR Playbook OAuth Access and Refresh Token Revocation for Connected App) AND XQL(Revoked-Token Replay Returns 401 invalid_token Closed-Loop Proof) observed on the same connected_app and oauth_token_id within the run window — stitches the full closed loop trusted-token -> mass CRM export -> query-job deletion -> automated access+refresh token revocation -> revoked-token replay rejected 401 invalid_token into a SINGLE post-consent OAuth-token-abuse incident. The incident's terminal assertion is that the XSOAR auto-revoke playbook FIRED and CLOSED: the token that ran the export is verifiably dead because the subsequent replay returns 401 invalid_token, satisfying the F5 closed-loop response KPI. Forced re-authentication for affected admins is attached as corroborating remediation evidence; a benign Connected App whose token was NOT revoked is the blast-radius negative control.

threat_scenarios.name: Auto-Revoke OAuth Tokens on Connected-App Abuse — Closed-Loop Response Validation
threat_scenarios.description: Proves Cortex does not merely detect the Salesloft-Drift-style Connected-App token abuse but that an XSOAR playbook automatically revokes the access + refresh token and forces re-auth, and that the revoke is verifiable: a replay with the stale token returns 401 invalid_token. The correlation asserts the whole chain is one incident and the token is dead — the F5 Automation & Workflow closed-loop KPI.

threat_steps.objective: On the mass-export behavioral anomaly, the XSOAR auto-revoke playbook fires and revokes BOTH the access and refresh token for the offending Connected App.
preconditions: SaaS/CASB collector ingesting Salesforce event monitoring into cloud_audit_logs.
XSOAR auto-revoke playbook wired to the Connected-App-abuse trigger.
steps: Drive the high-volume Bulk API export on the trusted Connected-App token.
Observe the mass-export ABIOC fire and the auto-revoke playbook execute.
Confirm the revocation event revokes both access and refresh token types.
success_criteria: ABIOC `Connected-App OAuth Token Mass-Export Deviation Triggering Auto-Revoke` fires.
Validation XQL shows revoked_token_types >= 2 (access + refresh) sourced from cortex-xsoar-playbook.
Forced-re-auth requirement is applied to affected admins.

threat_steps.objective: The revoke is verifiable end-to-end: a replay call carrying the revoked token returns 401 invalid_token and CR-CLOUD-0007 raises one closed-loop incident.
preconditions: TS-CLOUD-007A completed (token revoked by the playbook).
steps: Replay a Bulk API call with the revoked Connected-App token.
Observe Salesforce reject it with HTTP 401 invalid_token.
Confirm CR-CLOUD-0007 stitches export -> erase -> revoke -> 401-replay into one incident.
success_criteria: Validation XQL `Revoked-Token Replay Returns 401 invalid_token Closed-Loop Proof` returns >= 1 row.
Correlation CR-CLOUD-0007 raises one incident whose terminal assertion is that the token is dead.

threat_steps.objective: Blast-radius negative control: a benign Connected App's tokens are NOT revoked and its calls continue to succeed.
preconditions: A second, benign Connected App with normal low-volume Bulk API activity.
steps: Run normal low-volume activity on the benign Connected App during the run.
Confirm no revocation event targets the benign app's oauth_token_id.
Confirm the benign app's subsequent calls return 200, not 401.
success_criteria: No OAuthToken revoke event references the benign Connected App.
The benign app produces no 401 invalid_token replay row.

preventive_controls: Scope Connected-App OAuth grants to least privilege and cap Bulk API row/object quotas per integration identity so a stolen token cannot mass-export the CRM.
Require admin approval + short token lifetimes and refresh-token rotation for third-party Connected Apps (Drift-class integrations), and monitor consented app inventory for drift.
Pre-stage an XSOAR auto-revoke playbook keyed on Connected-App abuse so response is automated, not a manual runbook.
detection_engineering: Let Cortex auto-tune an ABIOC on per-Connected-App Bulk API volume and object-diversity rather than hand-authoring a static threshold.
Alert on export-then-erase sequences (query/queryAll followed by deleteJob) by one oauth_token_id — the anti-forensics tell.

Validate the closed loop: assert an OAuthToken revoke event for both token types AND a subsequent 401 invalid_token replay for the same oauth_token_id, so the playbook's effect is verified, not assumed.
